'''William J. Samford Hall''' is a structure on the campus of [[Auburn University]] in [[Auburn, Alabama|Auburn]], [[Alabama]].  It is an icon of [[Auburn University]] and houses the school's administration.  The building is named for [[William J. Samford]], the [[List of Governors of Alabama|Governor of Alabama]] from 1900 to 1901.

==History==
[[Image:1890s Samford Hall Auburn Alabama.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Samford Hall in the 1890s]]
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[Image:Samford Hall Cornerstone.png|thumb|right|250px|Cornerstone of Samford Hall]] -->

When Auburn University (as East Alabama Male College) opened in 1859, classes were held in a structure named "Old Main" on the current site of Samford Hall.  On June 24, 1887, Old Main was destroyed by fire.  The following year, Samford Hall (then simply known as the "Main Building") was constructed, using, in part, bricks salvaged from the ruins of Old Main.  The design of Samford Hall roughly mirrored that of Old Main, except that Samford Hall had two main entrances instead of Old Main's one, and on Samford one of the two [[flanking tower]]s was considerably taller and was constructed to contain a clock.<ref name="loguesimms">Mickey Logue and Jack Simms, ''Auburn, A Pictorial History of the Loveliest Village'' (Auburn: s.n., 1996), Mollie Hollifield, ''Auburn: Loveliest Village of the Plain'' (S.l.: s.n., 1955)</ref>  In 1889, a [[clockworks]] and [[Bell (instrument)|bell]] were added to the taller tower.<ref name="dennig">Brian Dennig, ''[http://www.auburn.edu/~dennibr/samfordbelltower.html Samford Hall Clock Tower and Samford Carillon] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070126102950/http://www.auburn.edu/~dennibr/samfordbelltower.html |date=2007-01-26 }}'', accessed March 11, 2007.</ref>

[[Image:Samford Hall (rear).png|left|thumb|Rear side of Samford Hall]]

Through the late 19th century, Samford Hall was the college's main classroom building and contained the library. In May 1929, the building was officially named for [[William J. Samford]].<ref>Auburn University Libraries, ''[http://www.lib.auburn.edu/arch/buildings/samford_hall1.htm History of Samford Hall]'', accessed March 11, 2007.</ref>  In 1941, the tower's mechanical clock was converted to run on electricity, and in 1977, a [[carillon]] was added.  Samford Hall underwent major renovations in 1971, and the original clockworks were replaced in 1995.<ref name="summerford">Roy Summerford, ''[http://www.auburn.edu/administration/univrel/news/archive/1995news/199504news/19950428auclock.txt Auburn University's "Big Sam" Gets His Hands Back]'', Auburn University News Release, April 27, 1995, accessed March 11, 2007.</ref>  Today, Samford Hall houses the school's administration, accounting, planning, and public relations offices.<ref>Auburn University Libraries, ''[http://www.lib.auburn.edu/arch/buildings/samford_hall.htm Samford Hall]'', accessed March 11, 2007.</ref>

==Clock tower==
[[Image:William J. Samford Hall.jpg|300px|thumb|right|Samford Hall at night]]
Samford Hall's clock tower is the most recognized part of the building.  The original clockworks were built by the Seth Thomas Clock Company of [[Thomaston, Connecticut]].  These clockworks were replaced in 1995 by a clock and electronic carillon made by the [http://www.verdin.com/ Verdin Company] of [[Cincinnati, Ohio]].<ref name="summerford"/> A portion of the original clockworks and an original clockface are on display in the reception area of Samford Hall. The Samford Hall carillon plays the [[Westminster Chimes]] on the quarter-hour, and plays the Auburn University fight song, [[War eagle#War Eagle as Auburn.27s fight song|"War Eagle"]], a few seconds after 12:00 noon.<ref name="dennig"/>

According to a University legend, students once led a cow up the tower stairs as a prank.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://issuu.com/alumniau/docs/summer_2010?mode=a_p|title=Auburn Magazine Summer 2010}}</ref>

==Historic District==
Samford Hall is part of the [[Auburn University Historic District]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Floyd|first1=W.
